candidates.statement: Order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders, which the gateway surfaces as 502 on POST /v1/checkout. Traces show the gateway's checkout call failing because the downstream order call returned 500, so the checkout 502s are a propagated downstream server error rather than a gateway fault.
candidates.uncertainty: Root cause within order (db, payment, inventory) is not established; order-side logs/traces were not admitted.

report.explanation: Traces show every checkout 502 correlates with a downstream order POST /v1/orders returning 500; gateway metrics show 502s only on /v1/checkout with low latency, and topology confirms gateway->order. This bounds the fault to the order service's 500 responses, but the specific internal cause is not yet evidenced.
missing_evidence: Order service logs/traces for POST /v1/orders to identify the internal failure (db, payment, inventory) behind the 500
Order-side dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency
